sentences.text: This is the second bail application.

First bail application was rejected vide order dated 31.7.2019
by a reasoned order.

sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri Shamsher Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Apul Misra, learned counsel for the complainant, Sri Sunil Srivastava, learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text: 3. The applicant has approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.337 of 2018, under Sections 304B, 498A I.P.C. and 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station-Chhaprauli, District-Baghpat.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text:
4.Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is husband of deceased and allegations against him is that his wife died otherwise than under normal circumstances within a period of three and a half years of her marriage and a girl child aged about 6 years, born out of their wedlock is Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140724697/
1 residing along with parents of applicant.
5. This Court has sought a report from learned Trial Court about present status of trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Report has been submitted which indicates that there are 33 proposed prosecution witnesses, out of which only six have been examined and one witness namely Dharam Pal Singh has not appeared to record his testimony for the last five dates.
6.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that in case of conviction, minimum sentence is of seven years.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Applicant is languishing in jail since 21.8.2018, (i.e. about 4 years and eight months), there is no likelihood of early disposal of trial and the applicant undertakes that if enlarged on bail, he will never misuse his liberty and will co-operate in the trial.
7.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for complainant and the A.G.A. have vehemently opposed the bail application and submitted that there are serious allegations against the applicant and trial is proceeding,
therefore, bail may not be granted only on the ground of prolonged detention.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text: 8. Considering the above submissions and taking note about present status of trial as referred above as well as that applicant is in jail since 21.8.2018, i.e. about 4 years and eight months and other co-accused have been granted bail as well as that applicant has to look after a girl child aged about 6 years, in these circumstance period of detention is a relevant factor for granting bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text:
9. Let the applicant-Ravindra, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text: (iii) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text: In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text: (iv) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months after release of the applicant, if there is no other legal impediment.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140724697/
2
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text: (v) Applicant has to appear on each and every date before learned Trial Court and any application for exemption of his appearance on vague ground could be a ground for cancellation of bail by learned Trial Court without even issuing notice.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text:
10. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
11.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023.json

sentences.text: 12. It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only for the purpose of adjudicating the present bail application.

sentences.text: Considering the gravity of the offence, interest of justice will be served by directing the learned trial court to expedite the trial within a stipulated period of time.

sentences.text: The trial court is directed to conclude the trial within a period of six months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: The learned trial court shall proceed with the hearing on a day to day basis to ensure that the above stipulated timeline of six months is strictly adhered to.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: All witnesses and counsels are directed to cooperate with the trial proceedings.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: The trial court has also to be conscious of the rights of the accused persons and is under obligation of law to ensure that all expeditious, necessary and coercive measures as per law are adopted to ensure the presence of witnesses.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: Counsels or parties who delay or impede the proceedings should not only be discouraged from doing so but in appropriate cases exemplary costs should also be imposed on such parties/ counsel.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: The learned trial court shall issue summons by regular process as per Section 62 Cr.P.C. and also by registered post as provided under Section 69 Cr.P.C. to expedite the trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: The learned trial court shall promptly take out all strict coercive measures against all the witnesses in accordance with law who fail to appear in the trial proceeding.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: Counsels or parties who delay or impede the proceedings should not only be discouraged from doing so but in appropriate cases exemplary costs should also be imposed on such parties/ counsel.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: The police authorities shall ensure that warrants or any coercive measures as per law taken out by the learned trial court to ensure that the attendance of the witnesses are promptly executed.

sentences.text: In case there is a failure on part of the police authorities to execute the warrants or other coercive measures, the Senior Superintendent of Police, Budaun shall state the reasons for the same in the said affidavit and also show the steps taken to execute the warrants.

FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and his family members and according to the FIR marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the daughter of the informant on 25.02.2019 and after marriage applicant and his family members tortured her for demand of Rs. 2 lakhs and a motorcycle and on 12.04.2024 they have committed her murder her.

sentences.text:
Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submits, applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within five years of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but could not dispute the fact that from the post mortem report, prima facie, it appears to be a case of suicidal death and from the statements of independent witnesses it reflects that deceased was short tampered lady and often fight took place between husband and wife.
10.

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

sentences.text: 11. However, applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within five years of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but from the statements of the independent witnesses, which have been annexed along with instant bail application, it reflects that deceased was reluctant to perform her matrimonial duties and she always involved in her mobile and considering these statements, the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant with regard to alleged suicide committed by his wife cannot be completely ruled out at this stage.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 12. Further, post mortem report also suggests that deceased died due to hanging.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: Further, from the inquest report it reflects that informant was present at the time of inquest and he was one of the inquest witness but at that time he did not raise any objection and next day he lodged FIR of the present case.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 11 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 13. Further, applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 15.04.2024 i.e. for last more than six months.
sentences._hearing_file: Ravindra vs State Of U.P. on 11 November, 2024.json

applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

opennyai_summary.23_March_2023__decision:
First bail application was rejected vide order dated 31.7.2019
by a reasoned order.
9. Let the applicant-Ravindra, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iii) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.
In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(iv) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months after release of the applicant, if there is no other legal impediment.
(v) Applicant has to appear on each and every date before learned Trial Court and any application for exemption of his appearance on vague ground could be a ground for cancellation of bail by learned Trial Court without even issuing notice.
10. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
11.
The bail application is allowed.
12. It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only for the purpose of adjudicating the present bail application.

opennyai_summary.21_July_2023__facts:
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 13.12.2017.
The applicant is the wife of the deceased.
opennyai_summary.21_July_2023__arguments:
It is contended on behalf of the applicant that there were witnesses who have not supported the prosecution case on behalf of the State.
It is submitted on behalf of the A.G.A. that there is evidence to bring home the charge against the applicant.
opennyai_summary.21_July_2023__ANALYSIS:
At this stage, the Court does not propose to appraisal of evidence led before the learned trial court since it might the influence the trial.
The trial court has also to be conscious of the rights of the accused persons and is under obligation of law to ensure that all expeditious, necessary and coercive measures as per law are adopted to ensure the presence of witnesses.
opennyai_summary.21_July_2023__decision:
The trial is on foot.
There is likelihood that the applicant committed the offence.
The offence is grave.
At this stage, no case for bail is made out.
The bail application is dismissed.
Considering the gravity of the offence, interest of justice will be served by directing the learned trial court to expedite the trial within a stipulated period of time.
The trial court is directed to conclude the trial within a period of six months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
The learned trial court shall proceed with the hearing on a day to day basis to ensure that the above stipulated timeline of six months is strictly adhered to.
All witnesses and counsels are directed to cooperate with the trial proceedings.
Counsels or parties who delay or impede the proceedings should not only be discouraged from doing so but in appropriate cases exemplary costs should also be imposed on such parties/ counsel.
The learned trial court shall issue summons by regular process as per Section 62 Cr.P.C. and also by registered post as provided under Section 69 Cr.P.C. to expedite the trial.
The learned trial court shall promptly take out all strict coercive measures against all the witnesses in accordance with law who fail to appear in the trial proceeding.
Counsels or parties who delay or impede the proceedings should not only be discouraged from doing so but in appropriate cases exemplary costs should also be imposed on such parties/ counsel.
The police authorities shall ensure that warrants or any coercive measures as per law taken out by the learned trial court to ensure that the attendance of the witnesses are promptly executed.
The Senior Superintendent of Police, Budaun shall file an affidavit before the trial court on the date fixed regarding status of execution of the warrants/service of summons taken out by the learned trial court.
In case there is a failure on part of the police authorities to execute the warrants or other coercive measures, the Senior Superintendent of Police, Budaun shall state the reasons for the same in the said affidavit and also show the steps taken to execute the warrants.
The Senior Superintendent of Police, Budaun shall simultaneously inform the Additional Director General of Police (ADG) Bareilly Zone, about the aforesaid failure of the police authorities in the first instance to execute the warrants and coercive measures issued by the learned trial court.
If required, the Additional Director General of Police (ADG) Bareilly Zone, may issue an appropriate directions to ensure that the warrants issued are promptly executed by the learned trial court.
The delay in execution of warrants and consequent absence of witnesses is one of the principal causes of delays in criminal trials and has to be addressed effectively by all stakeholders.
The trial judge shall submit a fortnightly report on the progress of trial and the steps taken to comply with this order to the learned District Judge.
The District Judge, Budaun shall submit a compliance report regarding the status of the trial and the steps taken to comply with the orders of this Court after every month before the Hon'ble Administrative Judge.

opennyai_summary.11_November_2024__ANALYSIS:
11. However, applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within five years of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but from the statements of the independent witnesses, which have been annexed along with instant bail application, it reflects that deceased was reluctant to perform her matrimonial duties and she always involved in her mobile and considering these statements, the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant with regard to alleged suicide committed by his wife cannot be completely ruled out at this stage.
Further, from the inquest report it reflects that informant was present at the time of inquest and he was one of the inquest witness but at that time he did not raise any objection and next day he lodged FIR of the present case.
13. Further, applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 15.04.2024 i.e. for last more than six months.
Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
